methods.name: Stage-Progression
methods.rationale: Applies typical Series A → next-stage step-up multiplier (2.0x) to $115M total raised proxy.

methods.name: Peer-Median
methods.rationale: Median across 4 same-sector + same/adjacent-stage peers in Robotics & Manufacturing. Range: $1.1B - $2.0B.

data.narrative:
TerraFirma is a Series A robotics and manufacturing company that has raised $115M to date. The valuation analysis draws on a universe of 9 comparable companies—1 public (ticker: 277810.KQ) and 8 private firms including Divergent, Exotec, Locus Robotics, Generalist AI, Bedrock Robotics, and others in the same sector and adjacent development stages.

Two triangulation methods are applied. The stage-progression approach uses total capital raised as a proxy valuation baseline and applies a 2.0x step-up multiplier typical of Series A to subsequent-stage transitions, yielding $230M. The peer-median method anchors to a cohort of four same-sector, same/adjacent-stage comparables (Generalist AI at $2.0B, Bedrock Robotics at $1.8B, Dexterity at $1.6B, and Walden Robotics at $1.1B), producing a median valuation of $1.7B with a range of $1.1B to $2.0B.

The two methods produce a wide triangulated range: $196M (low), $965M (median), and $2.0B (high). The disparity reflects uncertainty around whether TerraFirma's growth trajectory and market position align with earlier-stage or more mature peer valuations. The peer-median method suggests later-stage comparables may be more relevant; however, the stage-progression method reflects the company's actual Series A position. A defensible valuation range of $400M–$1.2B balances these signals, with key sensitivities to revenue trajectory, competitive differentiation within robotics automation, and path to Series B funding.
